messages:
Maya: Quick q — flying to Berlin next week, want to bring two 20,000mAh power banks and a spare mini battery for camera. Anyone hit trouble with airlines? :airplane:
Tim: Carry-on only. Most airlines allow up to ~100Wh without approval. 20,000mAh (3.7V) is ~74Wh so you're fine normally.
Noah: Formula if useful:
```
Wh = (mAh / 1000) * V
=> 20000/1000 * 3.7 = 74 Wh
```
Jen: Had one pulled at check-in in IST once — they said mine wasn't declared and insisted it be in carry-on. luckily I moved it and they let me through.
Ash: Short checklist: pack power banks in carry-on, tape exposed terminals or put in pouch, keep them turned off, label capacity if you can. Some airlines limit number of spare lithium batteries.
Tim: Also worth checking specific carrier rules. I had to email a Korean airline for approval for >160Wh units once.
Maya: Good call. Any compact travel-chargers you'd recommend? Need USB-C PD + another USB-A for older stuff.
Noah: Anker 737 (GaN) worked for me. 65W on USB-C and passthrough is solid. If you need higher single-port, look for 100W GaN.
Jen: Pro tip: bring a short USB-C to USB-C 30cm cable and a little cable organizer pocket. Saved me at security multiple times.
ops-bot: Reminder: company travel policy — all electronics with spare batteries should be carried in-cabin. See policies/travel in the handbook. :memo:
Maya: Thanks all :thumbsup: Appreciated — I'll stash everything in my carry-on and label them. Anyone want my mini charger if I buy a spare? I'll bring it to the office before I leave.
Ash: I'll take it if it's cheap :grin:
Tim: me too if Ash backs out :stuck_out_tongue:
Noah: If anyone else wants to compare notes before the trip, ping me. I keep a tiny checklist in Notes for flights.
Jen: Safe travels! and bring a power strip? no, wait — not allowed on planes. bring a multiport charger instead. :sweat_smile:
